verdicts.why: Formal register label plus a contrast with patience (tolerance as a reaction deliberately withheld) matches the good-natured-tolerance gloss and stays inside the word; positive charge fits.
Describes a whole bent toward kindness and compassion, exactly the gloss, and the victor's-grace example shows that disposition; positive charge fits.
Plain praise for absorbing delay or bungling without souring is the gloss restated as force; both Austen examples show tolerance of an irritant.
Locates the fault in manner rather than feeling, which is what 'harshness of manner' says, and the formal-register claim is a usage fact, not a distribution claim.
Fastening the fault on the single trigger of delay is the gloss; the contrast with temper is about the word's force, and the queue example fits.
Same harsh manner as asperity, differentiated by plainness and the felt cutting edge; stays on the word and the negative charge fits.
Reads the gloss as a disposition (settled liability, not passing mood) and describes what attributing the word does; both examples show the disposition sense.
Informal, clipped register against abstract secrecy is a register contrast on the same trait, and 'mum's the word' is this sense; neutral charge fits.
Flat name for the trait, taking no view on what is kept back, matches the gloss and the neutral charge; both examples use secrecy as a trait of discretion.
Names the trait by its outward result rather than the keeping back itself, a word-internal contrast that fits the keeping-things-secret gloss.
Weights the not-caring half of a two-sided gloss and derives the faint reproach from that, which justifies the negative charge; the Austen examples fit.
Weights the calm, casual half of the same gloss and keeps the 'seeming' hedge, so the neutral charge against indifference's negative is plausible.

A respectable surface that shades rather than hides fits the misleading-appearance gloss; the OEWN example 'took on a different color' is a loose fit for deliberate misleading but is the synset's own, and the note itself is sound.
British spelling is a register fact; the tint-versus-cover contrast with disguise is word-internal, and the example shows a colour used to hide wrongdoing.
Outward form that actively misrepresents what lies beneath is the gloss, placed against the shading words in the family; the example fits.
Polish worked onto the outside, deceit of finish rather than concealment, fits the misleading-appearance gloss and the moral-sanction example.
Artful semblance framed as a form put on and worn fits the gloss, and 'under the guise of friendship' shows exactly that assumed form.
British spelling is a register fact; foregrounding the artfulness of something got up is the 'artful or simulated semblance' gloss.
Barest word naming only the outward form and leaving the misleading to inference fits the gloss and the 'semblance of authenticity' example.
Tracing the blemish to birth rather than injury is what the word does to its referent, and the resulting absence of blame justifies the neutral charge.
Damage kept at the level of appearance, against defect's judgement of faultiness, is the gloss's 'spoils the appearance' read as force; example fits.
Naming the place by the violence that made it stays inside the word and explains the weight; negative charge fits a burned area on the body.
Colourless name for the same loss chip reports, with no sound of breaking, is a word-internal contrast that supports the neutral charge.
Something gone rather than merely marked, with the abruptness the word carries, fits the chopped-or-broken-off gloss and the negative charge.
Gravity drawn from the gloss's break-without-separation and placed against chip and scratch keeps to the word; the mirror example fits.
Naming the spoiling mark as a fault so the bearer is judged wanting fits the gloss and contrasts cleanly with blemish; the scar example fits.
Impression under a blow without breaking is the gloss, and the comparison to chip places the word's mildness; negative charge is plausible for damage.
Informal and belittling register on the same blow-struck impression as dent is a register contrast inside the word; negative charge fits.
